children: A record $108.02-per-barrel diesel crack spread underscored the pressure gripping global fuel markets Tuesday. Shell
, the integrated oil, gas and refining giant, climbed approximately 2.0% to $94.87, based on the updated market quote.

Wars and export restrictions have sidelined nearly four million barrels per day of Russian and Middle Eastern diesel supply, industry executives told Reuters. Shell enters this crunch with its refining system running hard: the company achieved record 102% refinery utilization during the second quarter and generated $21.4 billion in operating cash flow.

That combination gives Shell powerful near-term exposure to elevated diesel and jet-fuel margins. The valuation picture demands more caution, however: the shares trade 15.67% above their $82.02 GF Value estimate, signaling that investors already expect considerable strength. Vitol also forecasts that costly fuel and tight availability could reduce 2026 global oil demand by approximately 1.5 million barrels per daythe same squeeze lifting refining profits could eventually weaken consumption.

title: Shell Surges as Diesel Margins Smash $108
